title: Allow profiles queries while the daemon owns the keyboard
description: User reports open-wbg-service profiles fails with the exclusive HID lock after starting the user service. Treat the report as confirmed; preserve serialized HID transactions rather than removing the lock. Make the read-only command usable with a running daemon while retaining direct access when no daemon runs.
acceptance_criteria: profiles returns live current/linked/profile catalogs with a running daemon; all daemon/CLI HID operations stay serialized; second daemons and manual switches still require exclusive ownership; standalone reads and explicit/configured serial filters retain behavior; test lock handoff and the real CLI with and without daemon/API; update README/help.
design: Keep the existing nonblocking lifetime daemon/switch ownership lock. Add a separate blocking cross-process HID transaction/batch lock; daemon holds it only while accessing hardware and releases it before waiting for events. profiles obtains only the HID batch lock, and switch obtains both. Use a persistent file descriptor in the hardware worker with an RAII borrowed guard to avoid reopening or allocating each tick. This preserves live direct profile output, all serial filters, and --no-api operation without adding an IPC protocol or cached/fake state.
close_reason: Separated daemon/manual-switch lifetime ownership from a blocking, RAII-protected HID batch lock. The hardware worker reuses its lock descriptor and releases access before idle waits; profiles acquires only batch access and releases it before stdout. Live reads retain current/linked/catalog output and serial filtering, work without HTTP, and remain serialized with daemon operations. Updated CLI help and README, including restart-on-upgrade guidance. Verification: cargo test --locked passed 22 unit tests plus the new full-CLI regression; cargo install --path . --locked --force and user-service restart succeeded. On the real 60HE v2, profiles returned unchanged Typing Profile and Valorant catalogs/app links while service stayed active; four simultaneous readers, exact/unknown serials, standalone mode, and a --no-api dry-run daemon all behaved correctly. Manual switch remains ownership-blocked; daemon PID/restart count unchanged during concurrent reads and status reported no hardware errors. Restored the normal active user service after standalone/no-API checks; user config/profiles were not edited.
